names.note: STRIKING as-of-date-skew evidence: the NSE shareholding master carries an off-cycle amendment dated 2026-04-11 (submitted 2026-04-13, promoter jumped 36.72% -> 41.71%, presumably a creeping-acquisition/open-offer event). yfinance's insider ROSTER (t.insider_roster_holders) shows the promoter-family rows individually dated 2026-04-11 -- i.e. yfinance's heldPercentInsiders (41.714%) matches the FRESH post-event filing almost exactly, not the 'official' quarter-end (2026-03-31) figure. Comparing against the wrong NSE snapshot manufactures a fake ~5pp 'drift' that is actually just two different, both-correct, as-of dates. The insider roster ALSO mixes entries from wildly different dates in one scalar (Lotus Global Investments Ltd. dated 2024-08-21 sits alongside rows dated 2026-04-11) -- heldPercentInsiders is not a coherent point-in-time cross-section the way the NSE quarterly master is.

summary_stats.hypothesis_assessment: The definitional-mismatch mechanism (insiders != strict promoter/promoter-group; the roster includes UNREPORTED-position and individually-dated rows) is directly confirmed. The as-of-date-skew mechanism is directly confirmed via KIRIINDUS's roster Date column. The exact ~2.5pp magnitude from the brief undershoots what was observed here (mean ~4.7pp on this 4-name sample) but Case A's BOMOXY-B1 pair (75.806% insiders vs 73.29% promoter = 2.516pp) lands almost exactly on the ~2.5pp figure -- so ~2.5pp appears to be a real, achievable value for SOME names, with the drift's actual magnitude varying materially name-to-name rather than being a fixed constant.

does_D56_label_declared_vs_paid_correctl.answer: NO -- it only flags a generic magnitude divergence, it does not distinguish direction/cause.
does_D56_label_declared_vs_paid_correctl.evidence: services/research/semantics.py _dividend_ttm_leg() (lines 129-169) computes only a SYMMETRIC relative divergence (_relative_divergence, abs(a-b)/max(|a|,|b|)) with no sign/direction branch. When triggered, it always emits the SAME hardcoded note: "The provider's dividend per share (Yahoo dividendRate) differs from the trailing-12-month dividends actually paid by more than 10% -- dividendRate can omit a special dividend, so the paid history is the complete figure." This note text assumes ONE specific causal story (dividendRate < ttm, an OMISSION). It has no code path or wording for the opposite case (dividendRate > ttm because it anticipates a declared-but-unpaid dividend) -- INFLATION. If a future name ever has dividendRate itself (not just trailingAnnualDividendRate) inflated by a declared-not-paid amount past the 10% threshold, D56 would fire and mislabel it with the 'omit a special dividend' narrative, which would be factually backwards for that case.
does_D56_label_declared_vs_paid_correctl.additional_gap: D56 is a fixed 10%-relative-divergence gate with no minimum-magnitude floor and no awareness of pending corporate actions (record dates) at all -- it cannot distinguish 'stale/incomplete provider scalar' from 'provider scalar anticipating a not-yet-paid declared dividend' from 'provider scalar lagging a corporate action it hasn't ingested yet'. All three collapse to the same generic conflict shape when they cross threshold, and stay fully silent below it (as happened for PFC).
